specifications.label: Length
specifications.quote: Z današnjim dnem je tako 7.976 metrov dolg slovensko-avstrijski predor je končno v uporabi
specifications.quote_note: Settled on 13 November 2026 from the source that ranks highest (ZAG, owner or official, then the latest). Shown before: 8176 m.

specifications.label: Tubes
specifications.quote: The current solution with only one tunnel and one track should last until 2040
specifications.quote_note: Copied from the source on 13 November 2026.

specifications.label: Tracks
specifications.value: twin track reduced to single track, freed space for rescue passage
specifications.quote: Perhaps most noticeable amongst the changes to be made shall be the reduction of the original twin-track arrangement to a single track configuration; the resulting space freed up is to be reused as an emergency rescue passage, improving safety throughout the tunnel.
specifications.quote_note: Trimmed to what the quoted source states. Removed as not shown in the quote: reduction from twin to single track with the space reused for rescue is stated as planned but the 2020 to 2021 dates are not

specifications.label: Opened
specifications.quote: Such was the importance of the Karawanks Tunnel that, on 1 October 1906, the opening ceremony was officiated by the Austro-Hungarian head of state, Archduke Franz Ferdinand.
specifications.quote_note: Copied from the text of the Wikipedia page, read on 12 November 2026.

specifications.label: Line
specifications.value: Karawanken Railway, Jesenice to Rosenbach (Trieste to Klagenfurt link with the Bohinj Railway)
specifications.quote: Upon opening in October 1906, the Karawanks Tunnel formed an important element of the Karawanken Railway, which was - together with the Bohinj Railway - constructed to connect the port of Trieste with Klagenfurt, the capital of the federal state of Carinthia in Austria.
specifications.quote_note: Copied from the text of the Wikipedia page, read on 12 November 2026.

specifications.label: Renovation 2020 2021
specifications.value: single-track conversion, evacuation route with lighting, power supply line, telecom/safety equipment, enlarged niches, cross-section repair, drainage renewal, dry hydrant network on Slovenian side, full closure Oct 2020 to Jul 2021
specifications.quote: preureditev na enotirni predor z zgornjim ustrojem iz tolčenca; … ureditev nove evakuacijske poti, vključno z osvetljenim oprijemalom; … Izvedba del v polni zapori proge je trajala od oktobra 2020 do julija 2021.

specifications.label: Renovation budget
specifications.value: EUR 115 million total (Slovenia EUR 50 m, Austria EUR 65.3 m), contractor Strabag
specifications.quote: The project has a total budget of 115 million euros, divided over the kilometers of each country, Slovenia contributing 50 million euros while Austria is to spend 65.3 million euros … The construction work is scheduled to begin on August 10, 2020, and will be carried out by the Strabag in both countries.
specifications.quote_note: Copied from the text of the Wikipedia page, read on 12 November 2026.

source_differences: Length: 8,176 m (current en.wikipedia) vs 7,976 m (older en.wikipedia copy on IPFS, earlier note also cites Structurae/Austria-Forum 7,976 m, not re-read here).
Structurae and Austria-Forum pages could not be opened, so their portal coordinates cited in the earlier note were not re-verified, OSM independently agrees with the stored anchor to about 3 m.

Wikipedia page read again on 12 November 2026: it states the tunnel was rationalised "from a twin-track layout to a single track". It does not state the number of tubes or the boring method. The year 1901 on that page is when the railway was decided, not the start of boring, so "bored from both ends, 1901-1906" stays unverified.
